official.application_cycle: 2027 intake (annual round; opened 1 July 2026, closed 1 October 2026)
official.status_note: Immigration New Zealand states applications for the 2027 intake opened 1 July 2026 and closed 1 October 2026, so that round has now closed. The 19 June 2026 announcement describes the programme as entering its second year and awards are made annually, so a further round is expected, but no dates for it are published yet.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship regulations state payment 'can be used toward tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs', and Immigration New Zealand describes the award as 'up to NZD$25,000 in course related costs and living expenses'.
benefits: Up to NZD$25,000 in course related costs and living expenses for one academic year
Paid in two equal instalments across the tenure of the scholarship
Usable toward tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs
eligibility: Be a former refugee or the child of a former refugee; former refugees include those who resettled in New Zealand through the UNHCR Quota Programme, the Convention Refugee pathway, or the Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship Category
Child means people who were born in New Zealand, but whose parent(s) or guardian(s) resettled in New Zealand as former refugees
Have successfully completed at least one year of tertiary study

Be enrolled or intending to enrol in full-time study in a health-related qualification, at level 7 or above and offered by a NZQA-accredited tertiary provider, with at least one year of full-time study remaining at the time of the award
Have the potential to complete the chosen qualification
Be a New Zealand Citizen, Permanent Resident or Resident visa holder and ordinarily resident in New Zealand
requirements: Pass all first-semester courses to receive second-semester funding
Submit a satisfactory report and an academic transcript at the end of each semester of the tenure
Take up the scholarship in the year it is offered; it may not be deferred or suspended except in exceptional circumstances with the approval of the Chair of the Selection Committee
Reapply each year to be considered for future funding
Not hold additional scholarships without the approval of the Chair of the Selection Committee, who may vary the value or tenure if approving co-tenure
Study full-time so the qualification is completed in the minimum time stipulated for it
If the scholar ceases enrolment or takes leave of absence, other than approved annual leave, the scholarship will cease or be suspended
documents: Personal and contact details completed in the application form

Proof of permanent residency via refugee background status, most commonly the Immigration New Zealand (INZ) issued Certificate of Identity or an INZ letter which confirms date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency
A CV including any prior health work experience

A statement describing your financial position: how you are currently supported financially, how you would use the scholarship, and what benefits and impact this scholarship would make to you and your family
A statement describing the potential impact you intend to have on the refugee health workforce and refugee health outcomes
A statement describing the strengths, attributes and support systems you have which would equip you to successfully attain your qualification and enter the health workforce
A personal reference, for example from a community leader, employer, teacher or other person who can speak to your attributes and potential impact on the NZ health workforce
An academic reference from an academic advisor or supervisor at your institution, or a teacher from your school
Copies of any other transcripts for all previous study, complete or not complete, including English Language, university foundation or preparation studies, NCEA or university results
selection_criteria: Impact of the scholar on refugee health outcomes
Impact of the scholar on the refugee health workforce
Impact of the scholarship to the scholar
Likelihood of successfully attaining the qualification
Priority will be given to those studying an in-demand discipline with a short lead time until entering the workforce
The Selection Committee may invite shortlisted applicants to attend an online interview; its decisions are final
coverage: Up to NZD$25,000 per academic year toward course related costs and living expenses (Immigration New Zealand)
Tuition fees, course costs, compulsory student services fees and other living costs (scholarship regulations)
Paid in two equal instalments over the one-year tenure
application_method: Apply online through Universities New Zealand using the Community Force platform once applications open
Complete the application form and upload the required documents through the Community Force platform on the Universities New Zealand website
Optional: attend one of the programme webinars to ask questions before applying
official.application_route: Online via Universities New Zealand's Community Force portal (universitiesnz.communityforce.com) during the annual July-October round; questions to nzrefugeehealthscholarships@mbie.govt.nz or scholarships-cf@universitiesnz.ac.nz
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be a New Zealand Citizen, Permanent Resident or Resident visa holder and ordinarily resident in New Zealand, and must supply INZ proof of refugee-background status
official.international_eligibility: Not open to students on temporary visas; the citizenship, permanent residency or resident visa requirement limits it to former refugees and their children already settled in New Zealand
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Health-related qualification at level 7 or above from a NZQA-accredited tertiary provider (Bachelor's, Master's, Postgraduate Certificate, Postgraduate Diploma, Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma), with at least one year of full-time study remaining at the time of award
official.duration: One academic year (awarded annually with a tenure of one year; recipients must reapply each year)
official.description: The New Zealand Refugee Health Scholarship helps former refugees and their children study health-related qualifications in New Zealand. Developed by the National Leadership and Coordination Service - a partnership of MBIE/Immigration New Zealand, the Ministry of Health and Health New Zealand - it aims to increase refugee representation in the refugee health workforce and improve health outcomes for former refugees and their families.
official.program_type: Government scholarship administered with Universities New Zealand (refugee health workforce)

applicant_utility.summary: This annual award gives eligible former refugees and their children up to NZD 25,000 for one academic year of full-time health study, paid as two equal instalments, but the second instalment is released only after you pass every first-semester paper. Applications run through Universities New Zealand's Community Force portal in a July-October window, so your INZ Certificate of Identity, full transcript history and two references need to be ready before the window opens rather than during it. The committee scores your likely impact on refugee health outcomes and the refugee health workforce, and the regulations state priority goes to people in in-demand health disciplines with a short lead time into the workforce.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Former refugees and their children who already hold NZ citizenship, permanent residency or a resident visa, have at least one year of tertiary study behind them, and are in the final stretch of a level 7+ health qualification aiming at the NZ health workforce.
application_readiness_checklist: Request your current transcript early and collect copies of every previous transcript, including English Language, foundation or preparation study, NCEA and any unfinished courses
Secure two referees before the window opens: a personal reference (community leader, employer or teacher) and an academic reference (academic advisor, supervisor or school teacher)
Locate the INZ Certificate of Identity or INZ letter confirming date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency, since that is the required proof of status
Draft the financial-position and workforce-impact statements in advance, covering how you are supported now, how you would spend the award, and the benefit to you and your family
Confirm your qualification is level 7 or above at a NZQA-accredited provider with at least one year of full-time study remaining, then register on the Community Force portal early
Attend the programme webinar when it runs around the application window for direct guidance from the administrators
common_rejection_risks: Failing any first-semester course, which withholds the second instalment for the whole tenure
Having less than one year of full-time study remaining in the qualification at the time of award
Falling outside the residency test - being unable to show NZ citizenship, permanent residency or a resident visa, or INZ proof of refugee status
Thin statements on impact: the committee explicitly assesses impact on refugee health outcomes and the refugee health workforce
Treating the award as guaranteed full funding - the NZD$25,000 is an up-to value set annually by the funder
Not being prepared for an online interview if shortlisted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the up-to-NZD$25,000 cap - the portion of fees and living costs it does not reach plus non-course expenses such as commuting, devices beyond required equipment and personal costs - must be funded by the scholar; the official pages publish no travel or relocation support.
document_audit: Proof of status is specific: the INZ Certificate of Identity or an INZ letter confirming date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency is the named evidence, so gather it ahead of time
Transcript expectations are exhaustive - every previous study, complete or incomplete, including English Language, foundation, NCEA and university results
References must be split into one personal and one academic, with the academic one ideally from your current institution's advisor or supervisor
The financial position, workforce impact and personal strengths statements are separate uploads; leaving any of them blank makes the application incomplete
All documents go through the Community Force platform, so file names and formats should be checked before the October deadline
alerts: The 2027 intake closed 1 October 2026 and the scholarship cannot be deferred or suspended outside exceptional circumstances, so apply in the round that matches your study year
Second-semester money depends on passing all first-semester courses
Holding another scholarship needs the Chair's approval and can change the value or tenure of this one
Full-time enrolment is required; ceasing enrolment or taking leave of absence ends or suspends the award
Recipients consent to their information being shared on NLCS and Universities New Zealand platforms to promote the programme
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one application on the Universities New Zealand Community Force portal during the July-October window with all statements, transcripts and references attached, then await possible shortlisting for an online interview before the offer letter sets out the two instalment payments and end-of-semester reporting conditions.
